sourceTitle: Using thousands of AI agents to uncover new leads in biological data
originalTitle: Using thousands of AI agents to uncover new leads in biological data
author: OpenAI

blocks.text: What if scientists could uncover new clues about Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s in minutes instead of months? Working together, OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps Research used thousands of AI agents powered by GPT‑Rosalind to analyze and interpret existing experimental data from millions of mouse brain cells in just 32 minutes. The agents connected the effects of gene disruptions with findings from scientific literature, uncovering unexpected biological connections that can help scientists understand disease and identify research directions for new treatments. The work shows how AI can help researchers explore more of what large biological experiments reveal.
blocks.en: What if scientists could uncover new clues about Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s in minutes instead of months? Working together, OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps Research used thousands of AI agents powered by GPT‑Rosalind to analyze and interpret existing experimental data from millions of mouse brain cells in just 32 minutes. The agents connected the effects of gene disruptions with findings from scientific literature, uncovering unexpected biological connections that can help scientists understand disease and identify research directions for new treatments. The work shows how AI can help researchers explore more of what large biological experiments reveal.
blocks.zh: 如果科学家只需几分钟，而不是几个月，就能找到关于阿尔茨海默病和帕金森病的新线索，会怎样？OpenAI、PerturbAI 和斯克里普斯研究所携手合作，利用由 GPT‑Rosalind 驱动的数千个 AI 智能体，仅用 32 分钟就完成了对数百万个小鼠脑细胞现有实验数据的分析与解读。这些智能体将基因破坏产生的影响与科学文献中的发现联系起来，揭示了意料之外的生物学关联，有助于科学家理解疾病，并找到开发新疗法的研究方向。这项工作展示了 AI 如何帮助研究人员更充分地挖掘大型生物学实验所揭示的信息。

blocks.text: Modern experiments generate far more data than scientists can thoroughly investigate. Researchers can now alter thousands of genes and measure their effects across millions of cells. But understanding what these results mean for human disease requires connecting complex experimental findings with decades of scattered scientific knowledge. This is where AI can help scientists uncover promising leads that might otherwise be missed.
blocks.en: Modern experiments generate far more data than scientists can thoroughly investigate. Researchers can now alter thousands of genes and measure their effects across millions of cells. But understanding what these results mean for human disease requires connecting complex experimental findings with decades of scattered scientific knowledge. This is where AI can help scientists uncover promising leads that might otherwise be missed.
blocks.zh: 现代实验产生的数据量，远远超出了科学家能够深入研究的范围。如今，研究人员可以改变数千个基因，并测量这些改变对数百万个细胞的影响。但要理解这些结果对人类疾病意味着什么，就需要将复杂的实验发现与几十年来分散积累的科学知识联系起来。在这方面，AI 可以帮助科学家发掘原本可能被忽略的有潜力的线索。

blocks.text: “We build cell atlases so that other scientists can make discoveries we haven’t imagined yet. AI could help more researchers explore these resources and turn unexpected observations into new questions to test.”
blocks.en: “We build cell atlases so that other scientists can make discoveries we haven’t imagined yet. AI could help more researchers explore these resources and turn unexpected observations into new questions to test.”
blocks.zh: “我们构建细胞图谱，是为了让其他科学家能够做出我们尚未想到的发现。AI 可以帮助更多研究人员探索这些资源，把意料之外的观察结果转化为有待验证的新问题。”

blocks.text: The team divided the analysis among thousands of AI agents powered by GPT‑Rosalind, an approach we call distributed biological reasoning. The agents examined a whole-brain CRISPR atlas, a dataset showing how gene disruptions affect different types of cells across the mouse brain. Each agent investigated a gene disruption, analyzed cellular responses, searched scientific literature, and proposed explanations for the results. Their reports were combined into a reasoning atlas linking genes, cellular effects, relevant publications, and possible biological mechanisms.
blocks.en: The team divided the analysis among thousands of AI agents powered by GPT‑Rosalind, an approach we call distributed biological reasoning. The agents examined a whole-brain CRISPR atlas, a dataset showing how gene disruptions affect different types of cells across the mouse brain. Each agent investigated a gene disruption, analyzed cellular responses, searched scientific literature, and proposed explanations for the results. Their reports were combined into a reasoning atlas linking genes, cellular effects, relevant publications, and possible biological mechanisms.
blocks.zh: 团队将分析任务分配给数千个由 GPT‑Rosalind 驱动的 AI 智能体，我们将这种方法称为分布式生物学推理。这些智能体研究了一个全脑 CRISPR 图谱，该数据集展示了基因破坏如何影响小鼠全脑中不同类型的细胞。每个智能体负责研究一种基因破坏，分析细胞反应、检索科学文献，并对结果提出解释。它们的报告被汇总成一份推理图谱，将基因、细胞层面的影响、相关文献以及可能的生物学机制联系起来。

blocks.text: The research team estimated that comparable human analysis and literature review, conducted one perturbation at a time, would take months to a year. The agents reproduced findings from human analyses while uncovering additional leads. Their assessments of novelty and scientific value also aligned with judgments from blinded human experts. These findings help prioritize further experiments needed to test the proposed biological mechanisms.
blocks.en: The research team estimated that comparable human analysis and literature review, conducted one perturbation at a time, would take months to a year. The agents reproduced findings from human analyses while uncovering additional leads. Their assessments of novelty and scientific value also aligned with judgments from blinded human experts. These findings help prioritize further experiments needed to test the proposed biological mechanisms.
blocks.zh: 研究团队估计，如果由人类逐一分析每种扰动，完成同等程度的分析和文献回顾将需要数月到一年。智能体复现了人工分析的发现，同时找到了更多线索。它们对新颖性和科学价值的评估，也与盲评中人类专家的判断一致。这些发现有助于确定后续实验的优先顺序，以验证所提出的生物学机制。

blocks.text: Some of these insights point to new leads for understanding brain disease. The agents identified unexpected differences in how two disease-linked genes affect brain cells differently, as well as a potential connection between cholesterol regulation and neurodegeneration. These findings could help scientists investigate how disease develops and where future treatments might intervene.
blocks.en: Some of these insights point to new leads for understanding brain disease. The agents identified unexpected differences in how two disease-linked genes affect brain cells differently, as well as a potential connection between cholesterol regulation and neurodegeneration. These findings could help scientists investigate how disease develops and where future treatments might intervene.
blocks.zh: 其中一些见解为理解脑部疾病提供了新线索。智能体发现，两个与疾病相关的基因对脑细胞的影响存在意料之外的差异，同时还发现了胆固醇调控与神经退行性病变之间的潜在关联。这些发现可以帮助科学家研究疾病如何发生发展，以及未来的治疗可能从何处干预。

blocks.text: “Sometimes the clues are already there, scattered across different fields—we just haven’t connected them. The possible link between neuronal function and cholesterol metabolism shows how those pieces, once brought together, can give us a new way to think about disease biology.”
blocks.en: “Sometimes the clues are already there, scattered across different fields—we just haven’t connected them. The possible link between neuronal function and cholesterol metabolism shows how those pieces, once brought together, can give us a new way to think about disease biology.”
blocks.zh: “有时线索早已存在，散落在不同领域——只是我们还没有把它们联系起来。神经元功能与胆固醇代谢之间可能存在的联系表明，一旦把这些零散的信息拼在一起，就能为我们理解疾病的生物学机制提供新的思路。”

blocks.text: Researchers can begin exploring these findings today. The reasoning atlas is available, allowing scientists to compare related genes, investigate unexpected responses, and identify promising leads to pursue. New discoveries often emerge when researchers from different fields bring their expertise together and connect familiar ideas in unexpected ways. AI can significantly scale these connections by linking new data with knowledge scattered across disciplines. The opportunity goes beyond analyzing data faster. By combining AI with experimental biology, human expertise, and scientific literature, we can help scientists turn more of their data into testable ideas.
blocks.en: Researchers can begin exploring these findings today. The reasoning atlas is available, allowing scientists to compare related genes, investigate unexpected responses, and identify promising leads to pursue. New discoveries often emerge when researchers from different fields bring their expertise together and connect familiar ideas in unexpected ways. AI can significantly scale these connections by linking new data with knowledge scattered across disciplines. The opportunity goes beyond analyzing data faster. By combining AI with experimental biology, human expertise, and scientific literature, we can help scientists turn more of their data into testable ideas.
blocks.zh: 研究人员现在就可以开始探索这些发现。这份推理图谱已公开，科学家可以借此比较相关基因、研究意料之外的反应，并找到值得深入探索的有潜力的线索。当不同领域的研究人员汇聚各自的专业知识，以出人意料的方式将熟悉的概念联系起来时，往往就会产生新发现。AI 可以将新数据与分散在各学科中的知识关联起来，大幅拓展这种跨领域联系的规模。这带来的机遇不仅仅是加快数据分析。将 AI 与实验生物学、人类专业知识及科学文献相结合，我们可以帮助科学家把更多数据转化为可验证的设想。

blocks.text: Big experiments, unexpected clues
blocks.en: Big experiments, unexpected clues
blocks.zh: 大规模实验中的意外线索

blocks.text: Some of an experiment’s most interesting clues lie outside the story scientists set out to investigate. In a dataset spanning thousands of perturbations, those clues can be easy to miss.
blocks.en: Some of an experiment’s most interesting clues lie outside the story scientists set out to investigate. In a dataset spanning thousands of perturbations, those clues can be easy to miss.
blocks.zh: 实验中一些最有意思的线索，往往不在科学家最初打算研究的范围内。在涵盖数千种扰动的数据集中，这些线索很容易被忽略。

blocks.text: The agents identified an unexpected difference between Tsc1 and Tsc2, two genes that work together to control mTOR, a major regulator of cell growth, metabolism, and aging. Disrupting either gene had similar effects in several groups of neurons. But in the cerebellum, which helps coordinate movement, Tsc2 disruption altered the activity of dozens of genes involved in neuronal communication, while Tsc1 disruption produced little change.
blocks.en: The agents identified an unexpected difference between Tsc1 and Tsc2, two genes that work together to control mTOR, a major regulator of cell growth, metabolism, and aging. Disrupting either gene had similar effects in several groups of neurons. But in the cerebellum, which helps coordinate movement, Tsc2 disruption altered the activity of dozens of genes involved in neuronal communication, while Tsc1 disruption produced little change.
blocks.zh: 智能体发现了 Tsc1 和 Tsc2 之间一项意料之外的差异。这两个基因共同调控 mTOR，而 mTOR 是细胞生长、代谢和衰老的重要调节因子。在多个神经元群体中，破坏其中任一基因产生的影响都相似。但在帮助协调运动的小脑中，破坏 Tsc2 改变了数十个参与神经元通信的基因的活性，而破坏 Tsc1 几乎没有引起变化。

blocks.text: That difference may be relevant to human disease. In people with tuberous sclerosis, abnormalities in the cerebellum are strongly linked to TSC2 mutations. While medicines that reduce mTOR activity can treat certain brain tumors and seizures, learning and behavioral difficulties associated with the disease remain challenging to address. The agents pinpointed a specific group of neurons and cellular changes worth investigating: which changes might existing medicines correct, and which might point to new treatment approaches? This gives researchers a more specific set of questions to test in the lab.
blocks.en: That difference may be relevant to human disease. In people with tuberous sclerosis, abnormalities in the cerebellum are strongly linked to TSC2 mutations. While medicines that reduce mTOR activity can treat certain brain tumors and seizures, learning and behavioral difficulties associated with the disease remain challenging to address. The agents pinpointed a specific group of neurons and cellular changes worth investigating: which changes might existing medicines correct, and which might point to new treatment approaches? This gives researchers a more specific set of questions to test in the lab.
blocks.zh: 这一差异可能与人类疾病有关。在结节性硬化症患者中，小脑异常与 TSC2 突变密切相关。虽然降低 mTOR 活性的药物可以治疗某些脑肿瘤和癫痫发作，但与该疾病相关的学习和行为障碍仍然难以解决。智能体锁定了一群特定的神经元及值得研究的细胞变化：哪些变化可能通过现有药物得到纠正，哪些又可能指向新的治疗方法？这为研究人员提供了一组更具体的问题，可在实验室中进行验证。

blocks.text: Divide the work, deepen the reasoning
blocks.en: Divide the work, deepen the reasoning
blocks.zh: 分工协作，深化推理

blocks.text: Could a single agent given the entire dataset do just as well as thousands of agents working in parallel? We tested this while keeping the model and resources fixed. As the workload grew, the single agent searched less of the literature, citing only 11 references at the largest workload, while the distributed agents cited more than 700 references. Human experts also preferred the distributed-agent interpretations.
blocks.en: Could a single agent given the entire dataset do just as well as thousands of agents working in parallel? We tested this while keeping the model and resources fixed. As the workload grew, the single agent searched less of the literature, citing only 11 references at the largest workload, while the distributed agents cited more than 700 references. Human experts also preferred the distributed-agent interpretations.
blocks.zh: 让单个智能体处理整个数据集，能否达到数千个智能体并行工作的效果？我们在模型和资源保持不变的条件下对此进行了测试。随着工作量增加，单个智能体检索的文献越来越少：在工作量最大时，它仅引用了 11 篇文献，而分布式智能体引用了 700 多篇。人类专家也更认可分布式智能体给出的解读。

blocks.text: Scientists have limited time and often focus on the strongest signals in their data. Distributed agents can help examine a wider range of responses, including subtle or unexpected ones, and connect them with relevant scientific literature. Running the agents in parallel allows many perturbations to be investigated at once. This helps scientists explore more of what an experiment contains and identify promising leads that might otherwise be missed.
blocks.en: Scientists have limited time and often focus on the strongest signals in their data. Distributed agents can help examine a wider range of responses, including subtle or unexpected ones, and connect them with relevant scientific literature. Running the agents in parallel allows many perturbations to be investigated at once. This helps scientists explore more of what an experiment contains and identify promising leads that might otherwise be missed.
blocks.zh: 科学家的时间有限，往往会重点关注数据中最显著的信号。分布式智能体能够帮助考察更广泛的反应，包括细微或意料之外的反应，并将其与相关科学文献联系起来。并行运行智能体，可以同时研究多种扰动。这有助于科学家更充分地挖掘实验中的信息，发现原本可能被忽略的有潜力的线索。

blocks.text: At the largest workload, distributed agents cited more than 700 references, compared with 11 for a single agent.
blocks.en: At the largest workload, distributed agents cited more than 700 references, compared with 11 for a single agent.
blocks.zh: 在工作量最大时，分布式智能体引用了 700 多篇文献，而单个智能体仅引用了 11 篇。

blocks.text: Finding the next experiment worth doing
blocks.en: Finding the next experiment worth doing
blocks.zh: 找到下一个值得开展的实验

blocks.text: A finding becomes more valuable when it points to an experiment worth doing. The agents found one such lead in DCTN1, a gene whose mutations cause Perry syndrome, a neurodegenerative disease with Parkinson-like symptoms.
blocks.en: A finding becomes more valuable when it points to an experiment worth doing. The agents found one such lead in DCTN1, a gene whose mutations cause Perry syndrome, a neurodegenerative disease with Parkinson-like symptoms.
blocks.zh: 当一项发现能指向值得开展的实验时，它就更有价值。智能体在 DCTN1 基因中发现了这样一条线索。该基因的突变会导致 Perry 综合征，这是一种具有帕金森病样症状的神经退行性疾病。

blocks.text: DCTN1 is involved in moving cargo inside neurons. In the whole-brain CRISPR atlas, disrupting Dctn1 increased the expression of genes involved in making cholesterol. The agents connected this observation with research suggesting that problems with cholesterol transport may cause cells to make more cholesterol. This raised a question for follow-up experiments: could DCTN1 disruption change how cholesterol is distributed within neurons, and could those changes contribute to neurodegeneration? If so, could restoring normal cholesterol distribution help protect neurons?
blocks.en: DCTN1 is involved in moving cargo inside neurons. In the whole-brain CRISPR atlas, disrupting Dctn1 increased the expression of genes involved in making cholesterol. The agents connected this observation with research suggesting that problems with cholesterol transport may cause cells to make more cholesterol. This raised a question for follow-up experiments: could DCTN1 disruption change how cholesterol is distributed within neurons, and could those changes contribute to neurodegeneration? If so, could restoring normal cholesterol distribution help protect neurons?
blocks.zh: DCTN1 参与神经元内部的物质运输。在全脑 CRISPR 图谱中，破坏 Dctn1 会提高参与胆固醇合成的基因的表达水平。智能体将这一观察结果与已有研究联系起来；这些研究提示，胆固醇运输出现问题可能会导致细胞合成更多胆固醇。这为后续实验提出了一个问题：破坏 DCTN1 是否会改变胆固醇在神经元内的分布？这些变化是否会促成神经退行性病变？如果是，恢复胆固醇的正常分布是否有助于保护神经元？

blocks.text: Human experts also considered this hypothesis novel, consequential and worth following up on. This example shows how connecting an unexpected result with existing knowledge can turn a clue into a testable idea, and potentially a new direction for treating disease.
blocks.en: Human experts also considered this hypothesis novel, consequential and worth following up on. This example shows how connecting an unexpected result with existing knowledge can turn a clue into a testable idea, and potentially a new direction for treating disease.
blocks.zh: 人类专家也认为，这一假设新颖、意义重大，值得进一步研究。这个例子表明，将意料之外的结果与现有知识联系起来，可以把一条线索转化为可验证的设想，甚至为疾病治疗开辟新方向。

blocks.text: In blinded comparisons, human experts preferred distributed-agent reports over single-agent reports 75% of the time.
blocks.en: In blinded comparisons, human experts preferred distributed-agent reports over single-agent reports 75% of the time.
blocks.zh: 在盲评比较中，75% 的情况下，人类专家更认可分布式智能体的报告，而非单个智能体的报告。

blocks.text: Scientists remain at the center of discovery. By uncovering more promising leads, AI can help researchers decide which ideas to pursue, design experiments, and interpret results. The goal is to turn more of the information in biological experiments into knowledge that, over time, can help guide the development of better medicines.
blocks.en: Scientists remain at the center of discovery. By uncovering more promising leads, AI can help researchers decide which ideas to pursue, design experiments, and interpret results. The goal is to turn more of the information in biological experiments into knowledge that, over time, can help guide the development of better medicines.
blocks.zh: 科学家始终是科学发现的核心。通过发掘更多有潜力的线索，AI 可以帮助研究人员决定哪些设想值得深入探索、设计实验并解读结果。我们的目标是将生物学实验中的更多信息转化为知识，逐步为研发更好的药物提供指导。
